title: Abaca Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Abaca Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Abaca nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in abaka, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Abaca nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your abaka (abaca) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which abaca nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a abaca nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest abaca nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in abaca

Abaca is a close cousin of banana and shows nitrogen shortage the same way. Old leaves turn light green, then yellow, and leaf stalks can redden. Plants stay short with thin stalks, small leaves and little leaf area, so the fiber harvest is light. Of all the shortages, lack of nitrogen keeps plants the shortest, with the least leaf area and the palest leaves. You see it most at this stage: from planting through the first harvest, and in old hills that are never fertilized.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in abaka
Most abaca farmers do not fertilize at all, and every harvest carries nutrients off the farm. Steep, eroded and sandy soils show it first.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage also stunts abaca, but it scorches old leaf tips orange brown. Bunchy top and mosaic viruses also give weak, yellowish plants, but with streaks, mosaic patterns or bunched narrow leaves. To be sure, A soil test and a leaf test. Get a soil test before opening a new farm and every five years after.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 after ring weeding, 60 to 90 cm away from the hill. Give ammonium sulfate at planting and at 8 months, then complete fertilizer at 21 months. Established farms get Complete 14 14 14 once a year before or after the rainy season, about a quarter kilo per hill (12 bags per hectare).

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.

To keep it away, fertilize every year, return stripping waste and leaves as compost, and plant cover crops on slopes. Let a soil test and the crop's color set the season's nitrogen. Split the nitrogen into two or three doses.
Potassium deficiency in abaca

Signs follow banana, its close cousin. Old leaves yellow from the tip, turn orange, then dry brown along the edges, and the midrib may bend. Plants stay short with thin stalks. Abaca suffers most from a lack of nitrogen and potassium. Plants without potassium were among the shortest. You see it most at this stage: from the first months through harvest, and in old hills that are cut often.
Why potassium deficiency happens in abaka
Fiber harvests remove potash every cycle, and most farms never return it. Sandy and leached soils under heavy rain lose it fastest.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium shortage also yellows old leaves, but the leaf edge stays green and leaf stalks show purple mottling. Leaf spot diseases show spots and streaks across the leaf rather than a scorch from the tip. To be sure, soil test for potash and a leaf test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Complete 14 14 14, after ring weeding and 60 to 90 cm from the hill. Where the soil test shows low potash, add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses. Give 200 to 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 a hill every two to three months, more as the bunch forms.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, fertilize every year and return stripping waste and old leaves to the field. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Phosphorus deficiency in abaca

Without phosphorus, abaca grows shorter pseudostems and narrower leaves, but the plant's height stays close to normal. As in banana, old leaf edges may yellow and die and young leaves can look dark bluish green. Roots stay weak. You see it most at this stage: early growth after planting.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in abaka
Acid soils that lock up phosphorus, and soils low in organic matter. Abaca does best at pH 5.8 to 7.0, so very acid soils bring it on.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage gives pale, not dark, leaves. Poor drainage and root pests also stunt plants. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Use Complete 14 14 14 at planting and after, and lime very acid soils. Where the test shows very low phosphorus, add 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0, following the soil test. Give 100 to 200 grams of Complete 14 14 14 a hill at planting and every three months.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put a phosphorus fertilizer in the planting hole and add compost.
Magnesium deficiency in abaca

Abaca shows it the way banana does. Old leaves yellow in the middle of the blade near the midrib while the edge stays green. Leaf stalks show purple mottling, and dead spots form in the yellow parts. You see it most at this stage: older hills, especially after heavy potash.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in abaka
Acid, sandy, leached soils and heavy potash fertilizer.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage starts at the leaf tip and edge as an orange scorch. Viral mosaic gives streaks and patterns on young leaves. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Apply Dolomite on acid soils, or Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite where pH is fine, following the soil test. Do not apply magnesium and potash on the same day. Give 50 to 100 grams of Kieserite or Magnesium sulfate a hill every three months, or Dolomite on acid soil.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite when liming and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Zinc deficiency in abaca

Abaca shows it like banana, where zinc is the trace nutrient that runs short most often. Young leaves come out smaller and narrower, with yellow and green stripes between the side veins. A purple tint under the rolled new leaf. You see it most at this stage: young plants and new suckers.
Why zinc deficiency happens in abaka
High pH or limed soils, organic soils and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart

Abaca bunchy top virus, spread by the banana aphid, is the bigger worry: it gives small, narrow, bunched leaves with dark green streaks along the veins and the plant stops growing. Zinc shortage has no dark streaks and new leaves recover after a zinc spray. To be sure, test spray Zinc sulfate on a few plants and watch the next leaves. A leaf test and soil pH help. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray Zinc sulfate on young leaves. Mix 2 to 5 grams in each liter of water. Follow the soil test for any soil dose. A usual soil dose is 20 to 25 kg of Zinc sulfate per hectare (about 5 kg of zinc), mixed with the basal fertilizer. It lasts two or three crops. A spray of Zinc sulfate at 0.5 percent (80 grams in a 16 liter sprayer), with half as much hydrated lime, works within days.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Petbowe Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** (33 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc) and **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming and very heavy phosphorus.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any abaca nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your abaka needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Abaca nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my abaka leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale yellow green plants that stay short, with thin stalks and small leaves. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in abaca?
items.a: Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 after ring weeding, 60 to 90 cm away from the hill. Give ammonium sulfate at planting and at 8 months, then complete fertilizer at 21 months.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in abaca?
items.a: Apply Complete 14 14 14, after ring weeding and 60 to 90 cm from the hill. Where the soil test shows low potash, add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in abaca?
items.a: Use Complete 14 14 14 at planting and after, and lime very acid soils. Where the test shows very low phosphorus, add 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0, following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my abaka lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the abaca nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
